full_judgment:
11. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, learned advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioners took me to the revisional-4 application, the impugned judgment and decree, the pleadings of the respective parties, the disposition of all the P.W.s and D.W.s and the documents exhibited by the parties and submits that the plaintiffs as well as the Government miserably failed to prove that the suit land vested in the Government as khas land during the S.A. operation in view of the fact that neither the plaintiffs nor the Government adducted any minimum iota of evidence including the khas khatian itself before the courts below in support of their contention nor did they disclose the source through which or the basis on which or the manner in which the suit land devolved upon the Government and as such the plea of khas khatian which is the genesis of the plaintiffs' claim falls flat and therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed. In this connection Mr. Bhuiyan drew my attention to Section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and referred to the decision of Geeta Rani alias Shamima Khatun vs. Bangladesh, 36 DLR (AD) 225; Bangladesh and others vs. Mallick Ali Ahmed and others 3 CLR (AD) 345 and Md. Kalam Mollah and others vs. Sheikh Samsu and others, 23 BLT 320, which will be discussed later on. 

 13. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan further submits that the plaintiffs as well as the defendant Nos.1-4 (the Government) did not neither specifically deny the accuracy or genuineness of R.S. Khatian No.259 (Exhibit-1/Ka of Title Suit No.214 of 2000) nor did they take any step against the said R.S. Khatian prepared and published in the name of Satish Chandra Das and as such the same has got presumptive value of correction in view of the case of Government of Bangladesh and others vs. Mrs. Mohsina Rahaman alias Joya as reported in 50 DLR 186, wherein it has been held that : 

 15. Mr. Bhuiyan next submits that the defendant-petitioners have lawful right, title, interest and possession in the suit land on the strength of their and their predecessors registered sale deeds dated 22.02.1961 (Exhibit-1 of Title Suit No.154 of 2000), sale deed dated 15.06.1982 (Exhibit-5 of Title Suit No.214 of 2000) and sale deed dated 16.07.2000 (Exhibit-3 of Title Suit No.214 of 2000) and those registered sale deeds being documents of title, will prevail over the so-called and non-existent S.A. khatian mysteriously prepared in the name of the Government. In this connection Mr. Bhuiyan placed reliance on 18 BLC (AD) 44; 13 MLR (AD) 6; 32 (DLR) 252; 5 MLR 374. In the case of Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan and others vs. Md. Nasir Hossain and others, 18 BLC (AD) 44, our Appellate Division unanimously held that: 

 16. On the question of burden of proof, Mr. Bhuiyan submits that the plaintiffs ought to have proved their case on the balance of probabilities without capitalizing on the weakness, if any, of the defendant-petitioners, but the Court of appeal below most illegally and in clear violation of the provisions of the Evidence Act, 1872 shifted the plaintiffs' burden of proof on the defendant-petitioners and as such the impugned judgment and decree being based on grossly perverse findings, is illegal and liable to be set aside. As to the point of the plaintiff's burden of proof, Mr. Bhuiyan referred to the decision reported in 58 DLR; I ADC 401; 8 MLR (AD) 41; 48 DLR 208; 39 DLR (AD) 237 and 9 BLT (AD) 66. 

 20. On the other hand, Mr. Shah Hossain, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party Nos.1-2 submits that on and from 14` April, 1956 the rent receiving interest of all the rent receivers in Bangladesh having been acquired by the Government under Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the SAT Act), the defendant-petitioners' claim of title to the suit land on the strength of a compromise decree dated 26.02.1957 drawn up in Rent Suit No.60 of 1957 between the then Zamindar/landlord Satish Chandra Das and his tenants Mohammad Mozahar Ali Miah and Azhar Ali Miah from whom the petitioners got the suit land by way of successive transfers becomes barred by law. In support of his submission, Mr. Hossain referred to the decisions reported in 31 DLR (AD) 323; 14 BLC 848; 38 DLR (AD) 93 and 20 DLR 699. Amongst the cited decisions, I feel the necessity to quote the ratio decidendi of the case of Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensing vs. Abani Kanta Chakraborty and others 38 DLR (AD) 93, which runs as follows : 

 22. Mr. Shah Hossain also submits that the defendant-petitioners produced and exhibited the certified copies of their title deed in support of their defence/claim to the suit land without any formal proof thereof and as such those secondary evidences in support of their title are not admissible in law within the meaning of Section 63 and 65 of the Evidence Act, 1872. To substantiate his submission, Mr. Hossain cited the decisions reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45; 41 DLR (AD) 97 and 14 BLC (AD) 132. In the case of Soya Rani Guha alias Soya Rani Gupta vs. Abdul Awal Miah and others 47 DLR (AD) 45, it has been held that : 

 23. In reply to the above submission, Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan submits that the certified copy of the title deeds of the defendant-petitioners are admissible in law within the meaning of Section 79 of the Evidence Act, 1872 in view of the fact that as registered documents those sale deeds carry the presumption of correctness of the endorsement made therein and if the opposite parties intend to dispute that presumption they are required to dislodge the correctness of the endorsement (Shishir Kanti Pal and others vs. Nur Mohammad and others, 55 DLR (AD) 39). In this connection Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that the decision reported in 55 DLR (AD) 39 being later in point of time will prevail over the one reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45. 

 24. Mr. Shah Hossain next submits that the S.A. Khatian prepared and published in the name of the Government vis-à-vis the suit land shall be presumed to be correct unless and until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. In this connection Mr. Hossain referred to Section 19(3) and 144A of the SAT Act and the decisions reported in 9 MLR (AD) 82; 30 DLR (SC) 81; 6 BLC 241; 33 DLR 126; 17 BLC (AD) 174 and 61 DLR 18. 

 30. The above findings of the lower appellate Court is erroneous and perverse on two counts, firstly since the plaintiff-opposite party Nos.1-2 and the Government claim the suit land to be the khas land of the Government, it is their bounden duty of proof their contention: There exists a large body of case law on this point. For instance, in the case of Md. Naimuddin Sarder @ Naimuddin Sarder vs. Md. Abdul Kalam Biswas @ Md. Abul Kalam Basiruddin @ Abul Kalam Azad and another, 39 DLR (AD) 237, it has been held that: 

 Furthermore, the plaintiffs stated in paragraph 7 of the plaint that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Rajbari Sadar, Rajbari (defendant No.4 to the suit) by his letter dated 12.03.2000 merely threatened to cancel their kabuliyat, but at no point of time their lease was actually cancelled, and the threat of cancellation as opposed to any actual cancellation is merely an apprehension which cannot substitute the cause of action of the suit as framed and therefore, the suit is premature and liable to be dismissed as being not maintainable in law as per the decision given in the case of Kamaluddin (Md.) and another vs. Secretary, Ministry of Land, Bangladesh and others 56 DLR (AD) 212, wherein it has been held that:
